The applicant filed an application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing the entire proceedings of Complaint Case No. 12833 of 2022 (Ruchi Vs. Ramu and others)

3. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State and Sri U.K. Pandey, counsel for the opposite party no.2.
Perused the record.
4. Perusal of record shows that the applicant was summoned by the trial court vide order dated 26.9.2023.
The applicant failed to appear before the concerned court.
The applicant is well aware of the pending proceedings.
The Application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. No.2218 of 2024 for quashing the entire proceedings of Complaint Case No. 12833 of 2022 (Ruchi Vs. Ramu and others) was dismissed by this Court on 5.4.2024.

5. The Apex Court in the case of Srikant Upadhyay and others vs. State of Bihar and another, (2024)
3 SCR 421 in paragraphs 25 and 26 has held as under :
"25.

entities.text:
Srikant Upadhyay and others vs. State of Bihar and another, (2024)
3 SCR 421
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The factual narration made hereinbefore would revel the consistent disobedience of the appellants to comply with the orders of the trial Court.

They failed to appear before the Trial Court after the receipt of the summons, and then after the issuance of bailable warrants even when the are co-accused, after the issuance of bailable warrants, applied and obtained regular bail.
Though the appellants filed an application, which they themselves described as "bail-cum-surrender application" on 23.08.2022, they got it withdrawn on the fear of being arrested.
Even after the issuance of non-bailable warrants on 03.11.2022 they did not care to appear before the Trial Court and did not apply for regular bail after its recalling.

It is a fact that even after coming to know about the proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., the did not take any steps to challenge the same or to enter appearance before the Trial Court to avert the consequences.
Such conduct of the appellants in the light of the aforesaid circumstances, leaves us with no hesitation to hold that they are not entitled to seek the benefit of pre-arrest bail.

26. The upshot of the discussion is that there is no ground for interfering with the order of the High Court rejecting the application for anticipatory bail rather not considering application on merits.
Since their action is nothing short of defying the lawful orders of the Court and attempting to delay the proceedings, this appeal must fails.
Consequently, it is dismissed."
6. In view thereof, the applicant is not entitled for grant of anticipatory bail.
7. Accordingly, the application is hereby rejected.
